names.ALPN_protocol: The application protocol the server selects, returned in EncryptedExtensions (§4.2, §4.3.1).
names.ALPN_protocols_Client: The application protocols the client offers in its ALPN extension of the ClientHello (§4.2).
names.ALPN_protocols_Server: The application protocols the server accepts in Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation (application_layer_protocol_negotiation, sent in ClientHello and answered in EncryptedExtensions), from which it selects the connection's ALPN protocol (§4.2, §4.2.9).
names.Client: The client, the endpoint initiating the TLS connection (§1.1).
names.PSK_KDF_identifier: The Hash algorithm associated with a PSK, the KDF hash of the connection that established a ticket or the one set when an external PSK is established, defaulting to SHA-256 (§4.2.10).
names.PSK_cipher_suite: The cipher suite for use with a PSK, which must be provisioned with an external PSK used for early data, which the server must select compatibly with the PSK, and which 0-RTT data must use (§2.3, §4.2.9, §4.2.10).
names.certificate_authorities_Client: The distinguished names of the certificate authorities the client accepts, sent in its certificate_authorities extension (§4.2.4).
names.certificate_authorities_Server: The distinguished names of the certificate authorities the server accepts, sent in the certificate_authorities extension of its CertificateRequest (§4.2.4, §4.3.2).
names.certificate_list_Client: The client's certificate chain, the CertificateEntry list of its Certificate message (§4.4.2, §4.4.2.3).
names.certificate_list_Server: The server's certificate chain, the CertificateEntry list of its Certificate message (§4.4.2, §4.4.2.2).
names.cipher_suites_Client: The cipher suites the client supports, listed in ClientHello.cipher_suites in order of preference (§4.1.2).
names.cipher_suites_Server: The cipher suites the server supports, from which it selects ServerHello.cipher_suite (§4.1.1, §4.1.3).
names.client_authentication_policy_Server: Whether the server requests client authentication, by sending a CertificateRequest in the handshake or after it (§4.3.2, §4.6.2).
names.identity: A PSK identity, the opaque label of a PSK sent in PskIdentity.identity of the pre_shared_key extension, a ticket or an external label (§4.2.10).
names.max_early_data_size: The maximum amount of 0-RTT data the client may send with a ticket, carried in the early_data extension of NewSessionTicket (§4.2.9, §4.6.1).
names.oid_filters_Server: The certificate extension OIDs and values the server's oid_filters extension of a CertificateRequest asks the client certificate to match (§4.3.2.1).
names.pk_Client: The client's public key, carried in the end-entity certificate of its Certificate message and used to verify its CertificateVerify signature (§4.4.2, §4.4.3).
names.pk_Server: The server's public key, carried in the end-entity certificate of its Certificate message and used to verify its CertificateVerify signature (§4.4.2, §4.4.3).
names.post_handshake_auth_policy_Client: Whether the client offers post-handshake authentication by sending the post_handshake_auth extension (§4.2.5, §4.6.2).
names.psk_key_exchange_modes_Client: The PSK key exchange modes (psk_ke, psk_dhe_ke) the client supports, sent in its psk_key_exchange_modes extension (§4.2.8).
names.psk_key_exchange_modes_Server: The PSK key exchange modes the server is willing to use with a PSK, against which it checks the client's psk_key_exchange_modes (§4.2.8, §4.2.10).
names.server_name: The name of the server the client is contacting, sent in the server_name (SNI) extension, used to guide server certificate selection, and required to be the same as in the original connection when a ticket is resumed (§4.2, §4.4.2.2, §4.6.1).
names.signature_algorithms_Client: The signature algorithms the client lists in its signature_algorithms extension (§4.2.3).
names.signature_algorithms_Server: The signature algorithms the server supports for client certificates, sent in the signature_algorithms extension of its CertificateRequest (§4.2.3, §4.3.2).
names.supported_groups_Client: The key-exchange groups the client supports, sent in its supported_groups extension (§4.2.6).
names.supported_groups_Server: The key-exchange groups the server supports, from which it selects the group of its key_share and which it may send in supported_groups (§4.2.6, §4.2.7).
names.supported_versions_Client: The TLS versions the client supports, sent in its supported_versions extension (§4.2.1).
names.supported_versions_Server: The TLS versions the server supports, from which it selects the version of its ServerHello (§4.2.1, §4.1.3).
names.ticket_lifetime: The lifetime of a session ticket in seconds, NewSessionTicket.ticket_lifetime; clients must not use a ticket whose age exceeds it (§4.6.1, §4.2.10.1).
names.trust_anchor_Client: The trust anchors the client uses to validate the server's certificate chain, distributed independently of the protocol (§4.4.2, §4.4.2.2, §C.3).
names.trust_anchor_Server: The trust anchors the server uses to validate the client's certificate chain, distributed independently of the protocol (§4.4.2, §4.4.2.4, §C.3).
names.sk_Server: The server's private signing key, matching the public key in its end-entity certificate, with which it signs CertificateVerify (§4.4.2, §4.4.3).
names.PSK: The pre-shared key in use, either established externally or a resumption_master_secret from a previous connection, input to HKDF-Extract to form the Early Secret (zero if no PSK is used) (§2.2, §7.1).
names.sk_Client: The client's private signing key, matching the public key in its end-entity certificate, with which it signs its CertificateVerify (§4.4.2, §4.4.3).
names.resumption_master_secret: resumption_master_secret, Derive-Secret(Master Secret, "res master", ClientHello...client Finished), which a NewSessionTicket binds to a ticket as the PSK for later handshakes (§7.1, §4.6.1).
names.client_application_traffic_secret_0: client_application_traffic_secret_0, Derive-Secret(Master Secret, "c ap traffic", ClientHello...server Finished), from which the client's first application traffic keys are derived (§7.1, §7.3).
names.server_application_traffic_secret_0: server_application_traffic_secret_0, Derive-Secret(Master Secret, "s ap traffic", ClientHello...server Finished), from which the server's first application traffic keys are derived (§7.1, §7.3).
names.client_application_traffic_secret_1: The client's next application traffic secret after a KeyUpdate, HKDF-Expand-Label(client_application_traffic_secret_0, "traffic upd", "", Hash.length) (§7.2, §4.6.3).
names.server_application_traffic_secret_1: The server's next application traffic secret after a KeyUpdate, HKDF-Expand-Label(server_application_traffic_secret_0, "traffic upd", "", Hash.length) (§7.2, §4.6.3).
names.protocol_version: The family of protocol versions the endpoints negotiate through supported_versions, TLS 1.3 and the older versions a downgrade would select (§4.1.3, §4.2.1, §D).
names.key_exchange: The family of key exchange methods: (EC)DHE and PSK in this version, and static RSA from earlier versions, against which the downgrade protection does not work (§4.1.3).
names.server_certificates: The identity scope of the server identities clients authenticate through certificates chaining to their trust anchors; open means the attacker may obtain a valid certificate for a server identity of its own (§4.4.2, §4.4.2.2).
names.Server: The server, the endpoint which did not initiate the TLS connection (§1.1).
names.random_Client: ClientHello.random, the client's 32 bytes from a secure random number generator (§4.1.2).
names.random_Server: ServerHello.random, the server's 32 bytes from a secure random number generator (§4.1.3).
names.offer_Client: The client's offer in its ClientHello for the parameters the server will select: the protocol versions, the cipher suites (AEAD algorithm and hash), the key-exchange groups with key_share, and the PSK and its psk_key_exchange_modes (§4.1.1, §4.1.2).
names.selected_parameters_Server: The parameters the server selects from the offer in its ServerHello: the version, the cipher_suite (AEAD algorithm and hash), the key-exchange group of its key_share, and whether and which PSK is used (§4.1.1, §4.1.3).
names.application_write_key_Client: The client application traffic key, client_write_key derived with HKDF-Expand-Label from client_application_traffic_secret_0 (§7.1, §7.3).
names.application_write_key_Server: The server application traffic key, server_write_key derived with HKDF-Expand-Label from server_application_traffic_secret_0 (§7.1, §7.3).
names.exporter_master_secret: exporter_master_secret, Derive-Secret(Master Secret, "exp master", ClientHello...server Finished), the secret behind keying material exporters (§7.1, §7.5).
names.handshake_write_key_Client: The client handshake traffic key, client_write_key derived from client_handshake_traffic_secret, protecting the client's handshake records (§7.1, §7.3).
names.handshake_write_key_Server: The server handshake traffic key, server_write_key derived from server_handshake_traffic_secret, protecting the server's handshake records (§7.1, §7.3).
names.per_record_nonce: The per-record nonce of the AEAD-protected record carrying the data, the padded 64-bit sequence number XORed with the sender's write_iv (§5.3).
names.additional_data: The AEAD additional data input of a protected record, which this draft fixes as empty (zero length) (§5.2).
names.application_data_Client: The client's 1-RTT application data (TLSInnerPlaintext.content of a record of type application_data), sent after its Finished under keys derived from client_application_traffic_secret_N (§2, §5.2, §7.3).
names.application_data_Server: The server's application data (TLSInnerPlaintext.content of a record of type application_data), sent under keys derived from server_application_traffic_secret_N (§2, §5.2, §7.3).
names.early_data_Client: The client's 0-RTT early data, application data sent in its first flight under keys from client_early_traffic_secret, whose security properties the document calls weaker than those of other TLS data (§2.3, §4.2.9, §7.3).
names.signature_algorithm_Server: CertificateVerify.algorithm, the signature algorithm the server signs the handshake with (§4.4.3, §4.2.3).
names.exporter_value: An exporter value, HKDF-Expand-Label(Derive-Secret(exporter_master_secret, label, ""), "exporter", Hash(context_value), key_length), keying material that TLS exports to the application (§7.5, §E.1).
names.early_exporter_master_secret: early_exporter_master_secret, Derive-Secret(Early Secret, "e exp master", ClientHello), the exporter secret defined for settings where an exporter is needed for 0-RTT data (§7.1, §7.5, §2.3).
